title: Gartner: The quantum threat is already behind schedule
key_facts: The piece is a contributed TechRadar Pro Perspectives column by a Director Analyst in the ITL Application and Data Security research team at Gartner; the author's name is not in the fetched text.
Gartner predicts that by 2030 advances in quantum computing will make conventional asymmetric cryptography unsafe to use.
Gartner research finds that 61% of organizations lack full visibility into their own cryptographic systems.
The author says well-resourced state actors are already using 'harvest now, decrypt later': collecting encrypted data now and waiting until decryption becomes trivial.
Data with a long shelf life, such as government records, medical files, intellectual property, legal contracts and identity documents, is exposed because the theft happens now.
Replacing algorithms is not a drop-in swap: larger key sizes strain older systems, signing speeds change, and more standards are still being developed.

Advice given: build an inventory of all cryptography, protect first the data that must stay secret after 2030, build crypto-agility (the ability to change algorithms and keys quickly) and set up a cross-functional Cryptographic Centre of Excellence.
The author says IBM, Amazon and Google roadmaps or breakthroughs on error correction and qubit stability show the timeline to a cryptographically relevant quantum computer is shrinking.

why_it_matters_hint: Organisations holding long-lived sensitive data are told to start replacing and inventorying their encryption now, because migration takes years.
